data.name: Ekamansh
data.gender_notes: Ekamansh is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ekamansh is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Eka' meaning one and 'Mansh' meaning god. This name signifies the belief in one supreme deity. It is a name that embodies unity and devotion to the divine. The name Ekamansh carries the meaning “One God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekamansh usually hope their child will grow to embody one god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes devotion to the one supreme deity.
data.etymology: Ekamansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ekamansh total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ekamansh carries a strong cultural significance in Hinduism, wherein the belief in a single supreme deity is a fundamental tenet. This name reflects the emphasis on monotheism, unity, and the oneness of the divine in Hindu philosophy.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ekamansh holds great spiritual significance as it represents the deep-rooted belief in the omnipresent, and oneness of the divine. It is a reminder that no matter how diverse and complex the universe is, there is only one supreme being who pervades and connects everything. This name inspires a sense of devotion, unity, and oneness with the divine, invoking a spiritual connection and inner peace.

historical_references.reference:
The temple at Ekamansh was built by King Bhagiratha in ancient India, around 6th-5th century BC, as a tribute to Lord Shiva. The temple was believed to be the place where the God appeared to the king after he had brought the river Goddess Ganga down to earth from the heavens.

Reference: History of Ancient India, Volume II. New Delhi: Tarasankar Sarkar.
historical_references.context: Temple built by King Bhagiratha in ancient India as a tribute to Lord Shiva

historical_references.reference:
Ekamansh is also the name of an ancient Indian city, believed to have existed around the 3rd century BC. The city was an important trading center and is believed to have been ruled by the Nanda Dynasty.

Reference: Indo-Greek and Indo-Scythian Coins. New Delhi: Oriental Numismatic Company.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian city and important trading center ruled by the Nanda Dynasty

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name 'Ekamansh' refers to a single pillar or a single shrine. This concept is popular in Hindu architecture and is often seen as a symbol of unity and strength. In modern times, the name Ekamansh has gained popularity beyond its religious context. It is increasingly being used in home decor trends as a single unique piece or a collection of decorative elements that symbolize unity and harmony. Additionally, Ekamansh has found a place in spiritual and wellness practices where it represents the idea of focusing on one's inner self and achieving mental and emotional balance. The name Ekamansh is frequently searched on Instagram for home decor inspiration, pinned on Pinterest for future home improvement projects, and sold on Etsy as unique home decor pieces and art.
